groups.passage:
Kizhi is an island on Lake Onega in Karelia, Russia, with a beautiful collection of wooden churches and houses. It is one of the most popular tourist [[16]] in Russia and a United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) World Heritage Site.
The island is about 7 km long and 0.5 km wide. It is surrounded by about 5,000 other islands, some of [[17]] are just rocks sticking out of the ground.
The entire island of Kizhi is, [[18]], an outdoor museum of wooden architecture created in 1966. It contains many historically significant and beautiful wooden structures, [[19]] windmills, boathouses, chapels, fish houses, and homes. The jewel of the architecture is the 22-domed Transfiguration Church, built in the early 1700s. It is about 37 m tall, [[20]] it one of the tallest log structures in the world. The church was built with pine trees brought from the mainland, which was quite common for the 18th century.

sections.title: 三、文意選填（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第31題至第40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
Generally there are two ways to name typhoons: the number-based convention and the list-based convention. Following the number-based convention, typhoons are coded with [[31]] types of numbers such as a 4-digit or a 6-digit code. For example, the 14th typhoon in 2003 can be labeled either as Typhoon 0314 or Typhoon 200314. The [[32]] of this convention, however, is that a number is hard to remember. The list-based convention, on the other hand, is based on the list of typhoon names compiled in advance by a committee, and is more widely used.
At the very beginning, only [[33]] names were used because at that time typhoons were named after girlfriends or wives of the experts on the committee. In 1979, however, male names were also included because women protested against the original naming [[34]] for reasons of gender equality.
In Asia, Western names were used until 2000 when the committee decided to use Asian names to [[35]] Asians’ awareness of typhoons. The names were chosen from a name pool [[36]] of 140 names, 10 each from the 14 members of the committee. Each country has its unique naming preferences. Korea and Japan [[37]] animal names and China likes names of gods such as Longwang (dragon king) and Fengshen (god of the wind).
After the 140 names are all used in order, they will be [[38]]. But the names can be changed. If a member country suffers great damage from a certain typhoon, it can [[39]] that the name of the typhoon be deleted from the list at the annual committee meeting. For example, the names of Nabi by South Korea, and Longwang by China were [[40]] with other names in 2007. The deletion of both names was due to the severe damage caused by the typhoons bearing the names.

tags.topic: how typhoons are named: number-based and list-based conventions, Asian name lists and name retirement

sections.title: 四、閱讀測驗（占32分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41題至第56題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得2分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
The kilt is a skirt traditionally worn by Scottish men. It is a tailored garment that is wrapped around the wearer’s body at the waist starting from one side, around the front and back and across the front again to the opposite side. The overlapping layers in front are called “aprons.” Usually, the kilt covers the body from the waist down to just above the knees. A properly made kilt should not be so loose that the wearer can easily twist the kilt around the body, nor should it be so tight that it causes bulging of the fabric where it is buckled. Underwear may be worn as one prefers.
One of the most distinctive features of the kilt is the pattern of squares, or sett, it exhibits. The association of particular patterns with individual families can be traced back hundreds of years. Then in the Victorian era (19th century), weaving companies began to systematically record and formalize the system of setts for commercial purposes. Today there are also setts for States and Provinces, schools and universities, and general patterns that anybody can wear.
The kilt can be worn with accessories. On the front apron, there is often a kilt pin, topped with a small decorative family symbol. A small knife can be worn with the kilt too. It typically comes in a very wide variety, from fairly plain to quite elaborate silver- and jewel-ornamented designs. The kilt can also be worn with a sporran, which is the Gaelic word for pouch or purse.

groups.passage:
Wesla Whitfield, a famous jazz singer, has a unique style and life story, so I decided to see one of her performances and interview her for my column.
I went to a nightclub in New York and watched the stage lights go up. After the band played an introduction, Wesla Whitfield wheeled herself onstage in a wheelchair. As she sang, Whitfield’s voice was so powerful and soulful that everyone in the room forgot the wheelchair was even there.
At 57, Whitfield is small and pretty, witty and humble, persistent and philosophical. Raised in California, Whitfield began performing in public at age 18, when she took a job as a singing waitress at a pizza parlor. After studying classical music in college, she moved to San Francisco and went on to sing with the San Francisco Opera Chorus.
Walking home from rehearsal at age 29, she was caught in the midst of a random shooting that left her paralyzed from the waist down. I asked how she dealt with the realization that she’d never walk again, and she confessed that initially she didn’t want to face it. After a year of depression she tried to kill herself. She was then admitted to a hospital for treatment, where she was able to recover.
Whitfield said she came to understand that the only thing she had lost in this misfortunate event was the ability to walk. She still possessed her most valuable asset—her mind. Pointing to her head, she said, “Everything important is in here. The only real disability in life is losing your mind.” When I asked if she was angry about what she had lost, she admitted to being frustrated occasionally, “especially when everybody’s dancing, because I love to dance. But <u>when that happens</u> I just remove myself so I can focus instead on what I can do.”

options.B: When Wesla is singing on the stage.
options.C: When Wesla is going out in her wheelchair.
options.D: When Wesla is watching other people dancing.

options.C: Acquire a skill so that you can still be successful and famous.

tags.topic: jazz singer Wesla Whitfield, paralyzed by a random shooting, on overcoming disability

groups.passage:
Forks trace their origins back to the ancient Greeks. Forks at that time were fairly large with two tines that aided in the carving of meat in the kitchen. The tines prevented meat from twisting or moving during carving and allowed food to slide off more easily than it would with a knife.
By the 7th century A.D., royal courts of the Middle East began to use forks at the table for dining. From the 10th through the 13th centuries, forks were fairly common among the wealthy in Byzantium. In the 11th century, a Byzantine wife brought forks to Italy; however, they were not widely adopted there until the 16th century. Then in 1533, forks were brought from Italy to France. The French were also slow to accept forks, for using them was thought to be awkward.
In 1608, forks were brought to England by Thomas Coryate, who saw them during his travels in Italy. The English first ridiculed forks as being unnecessary. “Why should a person need a fork when God had given him hands?” they asked. Slowly, however, forks came to be adopted by the wealthy as a symbol of their social status. They were prized possessions made of expensive materials intended to impress guests. By the mid 1600s, eating with forks was considered fashionable among the wealthy British.
Early table forks were modeled after kitchen forks, but small pieces of food often fell through the two tines or slipped off easily. In late 17th century France, larger forks with four curved tines were developed. The additional tines made diners less likely to drop food, and the curved tines served as a scoop so people did not have to constantly switch to a spoon while eating. By the early 19th century, four-tined forks had also been developed in Germany and England and slowly began to spread to America.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.C: The history of using forks for dining.
options.D: The development of fork-related table manners.

options.B: Wealthy British thought it awkward to use their hands to eat.
options.C: Wealthy British gave special forks to the nobles as luxurious gifts.
options.D: Wealthy British considered dining with forks a sign of social status.

questions.stem: Why were forks made into a curved shape?

options.A: They could be used to scoop food as well.
options.B: They looked more fashionable in this way.
options.C: They were designed in this way for export to the US.
options.D: They ensured the meat would not twist while being cut.

tags.topic: the history of the dining fork from ancient Greece to Europe and America

groups.passage:
Animals are a favorite subject of many photographers. Cats, dogs, and other pets top the list, followed by zoo animals. However, because it’s hard to get them to sit still and “perform on command,” some professional photographers refuse to photograph pets.
One way to get an appealing portrait of a cat or dog is to hold a biscuit or treat above the camera. The animal’s longing look toward the food will be captured by the camera, but the treat won’t appear in the picture because it’s out of the camera’s range. When you show the picture to your friends afterwards, they’ll be impressed by your pet’s loving expression.
If you are using fast film, you can take some good, quick shots of a pet by simply snapping a picture right after calling its name. You’ll get a different expression from your pet using this technique. Depending on your pet’s mood, the picture will capture an interested, curious expression or possibly a look of annoyance, especially if you’ve awakened it from a nap.
Taking pictures of zoo animals requires a little more patience. After all, you can’t wake up a lion! You may have to wait for a while until the animal does something interesting or moves into a position for you to get a good shot. When photographing zoo animals, don’t get too close to the cages, and never tap on the glass or throw things between the bars of a cage. Concentrate on shooting some good pictures, and always respect the animals you are photographing.

questions.stem: Why do some professional photographers NOT like to take pictures of pets?

options.B: Pets don’t want to be bothered.

questions.stem: What is the use of a biscuit in taking pictures of a pet?

options.C: To arouse the appetite of the pet.
options.D: To keep the pet from looking at the camera.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of calling your pet’s name when taking a shot of it?

options.A: To help your pet look its best.
options.B: To make sure that your pet sits still.
options.C: To keep your pet awake for a while.
options.D: To catch a different expression of your pet.

questions.stem: In what way is photographing zoo animals different from photographing pets?

options.A: You need to have fast film.
options.C: You need to stay close to the animals.
options.D: You need more time to watch and wait.

tags.topic: tips for photographing pets and zoo animals

sections.title: 二、英文作文（占20分）
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長至少120個單詞（words）。

stats.source: stats-3.xls「英文科非選擇題分數人數統計表」第二題(滿分:20分)

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem:
提示︰你最好的朋友最近迷上電玩，因此常常熬夜，疏忽課業，並受到父母的責罵。你（英文名字必須假設為Jack或Jill）打算寫一封信給他/她（英文名字必須假設為Ken或Barbie），適當地給予勸告。
請注意：必須使用上述的Jack或Jill在信末署名，不得使用自己的真實中文或英文名字。
questions.scoring_notes:
【前言】（二）英文作文則是引導式寫作，採用的是簡函寫作的題型，滿分20分；考生必須根據作答提示，寫出一篇至少120個字詞的信函，對沉迷電玩、常熬夜、疏忽課業、並受到父母責罵的朋友，提出適當的勸告。今年的非選擇題試題命題得宜，選材內容貼近一般高中生的實際生活經驗，並兼顧時事，考生不難發揮。
【二、英文作文（二）評分說明】
英文作文採分項式評分（analytic scoring）（參見下表），分項得分加總之後，給予一個整體分數（holistic score），再依總分1至20分，分為下述五等級：特優（19～20分）、優（15～18分）、可（10～14分）、差（5～9分）、劣（0～4分）。評分主要依據為考生的作答內容，閱卷委員仔細評估其內容是否切題、組織是否具連貫性、句子結構與用字是否妥適表達文意，以及拼字與標點符號是否使用正確等。為確保評分之一致性，閱卷委員在試閱時皆必須完全熟悉及理解各分項的評分標準。分項式評分指標包含下列5項：內容（5分）、組織（5分）、文法句構（4分）、字彙拼字（4分），及體例（2分）。字數嚴重不足，扣總分1分；多寫，不扣分。若考生未按規定使用英文名字，扣總分1分；書信格式使用不當（如未書寫稱呼語及信末署名），扣總分1分（但日期非必要）。
表1：英文作文分項式評分指標（項目＼等級｜優｜可｜差｜劣）
內容｜主題(句)清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。(5-4分)｜主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。(3分)｜主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。(2-1分)｜文不對題或沒寫(凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算)。(0分)
組織｜重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。(5-4分)｜重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。(3分)｜重點不明、前後不連貫。(2-1分)｜全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。(0分)
文法、句構｜全文幾無文法錯誤，文句結構富變化。(4分)｜文法錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。(3分)｜文法錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。(0分)
字彙、拼字｜用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字錯誤。(4分)｜字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(3分)｜用字、拼字錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。(0分)
體例｜格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。(2分)（「優」「可」兩欄合併）｜格式、標點、大小寫等有錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(1分)｜違背基本的寫作體例或格式，標點、大小寫等錯誤甚多。(0分)
註：改編自張武昌等（民93）「英文寫作能力測驗規劃研究（VI）」研究報告。台北：大考中心。後經「95學年度學科能力測驗人工閱卷英文考科評分標準訂定會議」修改。

extraction.method: 題本文字以 Word 版 paper-2.doc（soffice 轉 docx，以 lxml 走訪 document.xml 的全部 w:r：底線 run 內的數字轉成 [[題號]]，第46題所問的底線片語轉成 <u>…</u>，w:sym Wingdings F0E0 轉成「→」）為主；以程式將全部 273 個文字欄位（大題與部分標題、說明、題組標示、選文各段、題幹、選項、選項庫）與 pdftotext -layout（paper-1.pdf，NFKC 正規化、去除空白後）逐一比對子字串，除第50題選項的箭頭外全部一致，反向檢查 PDF 文字層扣掉 JSON 內容後只剩題號與 (A)–(J) 代號；Read 看 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像確認段落切分、首行縮排、粗體／斜體／底線與第50題箭頭；答案取自 answer.pdf（pdftotext -layout）；評分說明取自 scoring.pdf（pdftotext 與 -layout，並以 Read 看 4 頁頁面影像核對），中譯英參考答案是沒有文字層的大括號分歧圖，以 pdftoppm -r 250 放大裁切逐字抄錄，英文作文分項評分表以 220dpi 裁切影像逐格核對；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英文工作表：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D）、stats-2.xls（英文工作表：選項分析 T／H／L 列與未答）、stats-3.xls（英文科非選擇題分數人數統計表），並以程式交叉核對（T 列標 * 的選項＝官方答案，56 題全部；T／L 列正答比例＝P／Pl，56 題全部；H 列正答比例＝Ph，55 題，第33題差 1；D＝Ph−Pl，56 題全部；非選擇題兩題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數 152,340）。建檔腳本放在 scratchpad，未進 repo。 查證（verifier）：另以獨立程式重新核對——56 題答案逐題對照 answer.pdf 文字層並以 Read 看頁面影像確認；全部 184 個選項、56 個題幹、8 篇選文各段與 10 個選項庫字詞以 token 層級比對 pdftotext 結果，並以 Word 版逐字（含全形標點、U+FE30 冒號）比對，除第50題箭頭外完全一致；Read 看題本 8 頁影像確認段落數（3／3／2／4／3／5／4／4）、空格位置、粗體／底線；中譯英參考答案以 pdftoppm -r 220 放大重新抄核分歧圖；作文分項評分表依頁面影像逐格核對；統計以 xlrd 重讀三個 xls，56 題 P／Ph／Pl／D、T／H／L 各選項比例、全體未答與兩題非選擇題各分數段人數／百分比全部比對一致。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 期別「94–110」一致：詞彙 1–15（15分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，15分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，10分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，每題2分，32分）、中譯英 2題×4分、英文作文 20分；第壹部分單選題 72分＋第貳部分非選擇題 28分＝100分。封面印「考試時間：100 分鐘」「單選題共 56 題」「非選擇題共二大題」。其他相符處：第一大題標題為「一、詞彙（占15分）」，與 spec changes「102 起『詞彙』改稱『詞彙題』」相符；綜合測驗、文意選填沒有「第16至20題為題組」這類標示（spec 記載 103–110 才有），所以這些題組沒有 group_label；英文作文「文長至少120個單詞（words）」與 essay_length_by_year「101-110」相符；作文評分為五項（內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字、體例），與 spec「106 起改為四項」相符。無差異。
validator warning「題號重複 [1, 2]」為預期：中譯英兩題題本編為 1.、2.，英文作文沒有題號（no 填 1）。no 必須是整數，所以沿用題本編號（與 gsat-103／104、ast-101 相同做法），另以 label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「作文」區分，label 沒有重複。
第50題選項的箭頭：Word 版是 w:sym（Wingdings，char F0E0），PDF 文字層是私用區字元 U+F0E0，頁面影像顯示為粗的向右箭頭。為了顯示與檢索，統一寫成 U+2192「→」（與 ref-111 相同），例如「Greece→Middle East→Italy→France→England」。箭頭前後沒有空白，照題本。

第46題問 “when that happens” 的意思，題本在第45–48題選文末段與題幹中都把這個片語印成粗體加底線，所以依 schema 原則在 passage 與 stem 中都標成 <u>when that happens</u>。其他格式依 schema 不保留：第26–30題選文的 World Hello Day（兩處）為斜體；第43、53題的 NOT 為粗體；閱讀題組標示「41-44為題組」等有底線；英文作文「請注意」句中的「不得使用自己的真實中文或英文名字」為粗體加底線。後兩項不是在問「畫底線的字」，所以沒有加 <u>。

段落切分：Word 版第31–40題選文第三段（In Asia, Western names…）在「…use Asian names to」後有一個強制換行，讓空格 35 落在下一行行首；PDF 頁面影像上是同一段落（該段左右縮排與其他段略有不同，但只有一個首行縮排），所以以一個空白接回同一段。第45–48題選文第三段（At 57, …）段末的 Word 換行（換頁處）已去除。選文段數：16–20 三段、21–25 三段、26–30 兩段、31–40 四段、41–44 三段、45–48 五段、49–52 四段、53–56 四段。
詞彙題空格：第6題題本的底線為 6 個「_」（______），其餘各題為 5 個（_____），Word 版與 PDF 文字層一致，照原樣保留。

題組標示：Word 版寫「41-44為題組」，PDF 文字層為「41-44 為題組」（中英混排自動間距），group_label 照 Word 版寫「41-44為題組」等，沒有改寫成 gsat-103 的「第41至44題為題組」格式（101 題本原文就是這樣）。說明文字的冒號照 Word 版：一、二、四大題與英文作文的「說明︰」「提示︰」為 U+FE30，文意選填、中譯英的「說明：」與「請注意：」為全形「：」。中譯英說明第2點在 Word 版前面有三個全形空白（U+3000）縮排，已去除並以換行分隔。英文作文 stem 照 Word 版寫「Jack或Jill」「Ken或Barbie」（PDF 排版顯示中英間有空白，是自動間距）。
逐字保留的原文寫法：第45–48題選文「the only thing she had lost in this misfortunate event」（misfortunate 為少見用法，一般作 unfortunate）；第49–52題選文「By the mid 1600s」（無連字號）。皆照題本，未更正。

中譯英參考答案：取自 scoring.pdf 第2頁「參考答案：第1題」「參考答案：第2題」的大括號分歧圖（圖片，沒有文字層；原註 1「{ }（大括弧）表示皆為可使用之字詞。」）。answer 取每個分歧的第一個選項組成的句子；完整分歧放在 accepted_answers[0]，記法「{a / b}」＝官方大括號中任選其一（與 ast-101 相同）。第1題第三個大括號是巢狀：上半為 {Taiwan-produced / Taiwan-made} {movies / films}，下半為 {movies / films} {produced / made} in Taiwan；最後一個大括號上半為 have {attracted / received / gained / obtained / drawn / won} {international / global / worldwide} attention.，下半為 have been internationally recognized.。圖中 Taiwan 與 produced／made 之間的連字號印得較長（像全形「－」），依英文複合形容詞寫成半形「-」。第2題官方參考答案沒有譯出題目的「也」（The locations where these movies were shot have become popular tourist spots.），照官方，不自行補上 also。

中譯英 scoring_notes：由 scoring.pdf 三處逐字摘錄組成，以換行分隔，【】內是本檔加的出處標記：開頭概述中「（一）中譯英，2小題共計8分…進行評閱。」與「今年的非選擇題試題命題得宜…考生不難發揮。」（概述原文中兩句之間是英文作文的介紹，已移到作文的 scoring_notes）、「（二）評分說明」整段（段末「請見以下說明1：」的註腳上標 1 已去除）、註腳 1（寫成「註：{ }（大括弧）表示皆為可使用之字詞。」）、「評分標準：」1–4 點。評分說明同時談兩句，無法逐句切開，所以兩題的 scoring_notes 相同。

英文作文：評分說明沒有官方範文，answer 為 null。題目沒有規定段數，tags 不填 paragraphs。scoring_notes 由 scoring.pdf 逐字摘錄組成：開頭概述中「（二）英文作文則是引導式寫作…提出適當的勸告。」與「今年的非選擇題試題命題得宜…」、英文作文「（二）評分說明」整段（含未按規定使用英文名字、書信格式不當各扣總分 1 分）、表1「英文作文分項式評分指標」（依 220dpi 頁面影像逐格轉成「項目｜優｜可｜差｜劣」一列一行；體例列的「優」「可」兩欄在原表合併為一格，以括號註明；標題的註腳上標 2 已去除），以及註腳 2（寫成「註：改編自張武昌等（民93）…修改。」）。表中「文法、句構／優」一格的文字層與影像在「錯誤，」後有一個空白（「誤， 文句結構富變化」），判斷是排版空白，已去除。

選擇題統計：stats-2.xls 只有 T 列以 * 標示正答，已核對 T 列 * 選項＝官方答案（56 題全部）。T、L 列的正答比例與 stats-1.xls 的 P、Pl 完全相同（56 題）；H 列只有第33題不同（stats-2 H 列 J＝100，stats-1 Ph＝99，四捨五入差異），high_group 取 stats-1 的 0.99，option_rates_high 照 stats-2 原值（J＝1.0）。stats-1 的 D＝Ph−Pl，56 題全部成立。各題 option_rates（加上未答）因四捨五入加總為 0.98–1.01，option_rates_high 為 0.98–1.01，option_rates_low 為 0.98–1.02（第31題 L 列加總 1.02、H 列 0.98）。omit_rate 為全體（T 列）未答比例，只有第56題為 1%，其餘為 0；H／L 列的未答（第35、40、45、55、56題 L 列各 1%）沒有收錄。stats-1.xls 的五組通過率 Pa–Pe 與 D1–D4 沒有收錄。

低答對率題目已複核，不是對齊錯誤（都是大考中心原始數據，T 列 * 選項＝官方答案）：第34題 P=0.30（F practice；16% 選 A request）；第54題 P=0.31（41% 選 D「To keep the pet from looking at the camera」，高分組也有 32% 選 D）；第17題 P=0.38（42% 選 A them）；第42題 P=0.39。本卷沒有負鑑別度，最低 D 為 0.37（第1、11題）。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 只有「第一題（中譯英，滿分8分，兩小題合計）」與「第二題（英文作文，滿分20分）」的分數人數分布，沒辦法拆到中譯英各小題，所以放在 sections[s5].stats 與 sections[s6].stats 的 score_distribution（schema 沒有定義這個欄位，沿用 gsat-103／104 的做法）。rate 為原表百分比÷100，分母是報名人數 154,560（含缺考 2,220；到考 152,340），已核對兩題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數 152,340，缺考列人數＝2,220。原表分數區間「9.00- 9.99」等的空白已去除；第一題 9 分以上的列在原表是空白，沒有收錄。小題層級的 stats 為 null。

標註判斷：第17題 some of which 標 grammar／relative_clause；第20題「…, making it one of…」標 grammar／participle；第21題 even 需由「took … for granted and even abused」的語意遞進判斷，標 discourse；第22題 where 在 though／because／where／when 四個連接詞中選擇，標 connective；第24題 neither 需由上文兩個提議都被否決推得，標 discourse／pronoun；第27題 Since then… has been observed 標 grammar／tense；第28題四個選項（quicker／sooner／easier／better）都是比較級，比較級文法本身不構成區辨，要由下一句 All one has to do is say hello to 10 people 推得 easier，所以標 discourse（key_phrase couldn’t be easier，不填 grammar_point；查證時由 grammar／comparison 改正）；第32、33題需由 however… hard to remember 與 girlfriends or wives 推得，標 discourse；第39題 request that … be deleted 標 grammar／subjunctive。閱讀第43題（NOT typically worn … for decoration）依 repo 慣例標 not_mentioned；第53題的 NOT 是題目本身的內容（為什麼不喜歡拍寵物），標 detail；第46題問 when that happens 所指，標 reference；第48題（most likely give … advice）標 inference；第50題傳播路線標 sequencing。s4g2 為專欄作者對爵士歌手 Wesla Whitfield 的人物介紹，genre 標 biography；s4g4 為拍攝寵物與動物園動物的技巧，repo 沒有用過 instructions，標 expository；s2g2 梵天把人的神性藏起來的傳說，標 narrative。sdgs：s2g1 為 UNESCO 世界遺產標 [11]（11.4 文化遺產）；s2g3 World Hello Day 促進和平標 [16]；s3g1 颱風命名（女性抗議改納入男性名字、颱風造成嚴重災害而除名）標 [5, 13]；s4g2 身障與憂鬱、自殺後復原標 [3, 10]；作文（沉迷電玩、熬夜）標 [3]；其餘無明顯相關，填空陣列或不填。

本檔新增的非 schema 欄位：section.part_title／part_instructions（第壹、貳部分標題，放在該部分的第一個大題 s1、s5；101 題本兩部分都沒有共同說明，所以 part_instructions 為 null）、section.stats（非選擇題分數分布）、group.group_label（閱讀題組的「41-44為題組」等題本原文）、sources.paper_word、question.stats.option_rates_high／option_rates_low／omit_rate。
